name: Chess
summary: Two-player turn-based board game on an 8x8 grid with six piece types, check/checkmate detection and special moves (castling, en passant, promotion).
entities: 8x8 board with files a-h and ranks 1-8
pieces: king, queen, rook, bishop, knight, pawn (white and black)
turn state, move history, captured pieces
special-move flags: castling rights, en-passant target, promotion choice
mechanics: White moves first; players alternate one legal move per turn.
A move may never leave the mover's own king in check, including moving a pinned piece.
King moves one square in any direction; cannot move into check.
Queen moves any distance along rank, file or diagonal; rook along rank/file; bishop along diagonals; none may jump over pieces.
Knight moves in an L shape (two squares then one) and is the only piece that jumps.
Pawn moves one square forward, two from its start rank, captures diagonally, and promotes on reaching the last rank.
Check is when the king is attacked; the player must resolve it. Checkmate is check with no legal reply.
Castling: king and rook move together when neither has moved, squares between are empty, and the king is not in, through or into check.
En passant: a pawn may capture a pawn that just advanced two squares, only on the immediately following move.
Promotion: a pawn reaching the last rank becomes queen, rook, bishop or knight (player choice).
Draws: stalemate, insufficient material, threefold repetition, fifty-move rule, agreement.
ux: Highlight legal moves on selection; show last move and check indicator.
Promotion picker for queen/rook/bishop/knight; captured-piece tray; move list in algebraic notation.
Undo/restart in casual mode; board flip; optional coordinates and sound.
Prevent input while an AI move or animation is running.
pitfalls: Allowing a king to be captured instead of ending the game at checkmate.
Not detecting check, pins, or a king moving into an attacked square.
Castling through check or with a moved king/rook; wrong en-passant timing.
Hard-coding queen promotion; wrong file/rank to board-index mapping.
AI choosing illegal moves; no threefold-repetition or fifty-move tracking.
Accepting a move while it is not that side's turn.
defaults: 2D board, local two-player, standard FIDE-style rules.
Algebraic notation, undo enabled, promotion picker, check highlight.
If an AI opponent is requested, start with a simple legal-move search, not a full engine.

ask.en: Who should the player play against?

suffix.en: Use local two-player mode on one board.
suffix.tr: Tek tahtada iki kişilik yerel mod kullan.

suffix.en: Add a computer opponent that only plays legal moves.
suffix.tr: Sadece yasal hamleler oynayan bir bilgisayar rakibi ekle.

suffix.en: Support local two-player and a computer opponent.
suffix.tr: Hem yerel iki kişilik hem bilgisayar rakibi destekle.

ask.en: Which rule set should the game enforce?

suffix.en: Enforce standard chess rules including castling, en passant and promotion.
suffix.tr: Rok, geçerken alma ve terfi dahil standart satranç kurallarını uygula.

suffix.en: Start with basic movement, check and checkmate; leave special moves out.
suffix.tr: Temel hareket, şah ve mat ile başla; özel hamleleri dışarıda bırak.

suffix.en: Use a wooden classic board style.

verification: Start position is correct and White moves first.
Pawn single/double advance, diagonal capture and promotion work; illegal pawn moves are rejected.
Knight jumps over pieces; rook/bishop/queen cannot pass through pieces.
A pinned piece cannot expose its king; the king cannot move into check.
Check is detected; checkmate ends the game; stalemate is a draw.
Castling works both sides and is rejected when the king/rook moved, a square is occupied, or the king passes through check.
En passant works only immediately after the double pawn push.
Turn alternation is enforced and the AI only plays legal moves.
Undo/restart restores board, turn and special-move rights.
